newsitem.title: ITALY: Analysts positive on Parmalat Beatrice buy.
newsitem.headline: Analysts positive on Parmalat Beatrice buy.

text.p: Shares in Italy's largest quoted food group Parmalat Finanziaria surged on the Milan bourse on Monday as the market welcomed its purchase of Canada's Beatrice Foods Inc, reassured that Parmalat has excluded tapping the market to finance the deal, traders said.

The Italian milk and dairy products group announced Friday it was allying itself with U.S. bank Citicorp in the deal, with Parmalat paying C$230 million for a 75.1 percent stake in the Canadian food group which has a similar milk and dairy-based product mix to Parmalat.
Citicorp will take the remaining 24.9 percent of the group which has a majority of its sales in Canada and the remaining near 20 percent of turnover in the United States.
Parmalat stressed that the cash for the deal will be met out of its own resourcs.

"Just looking at 1996 figures and taking the negative scenario of there being no synergies between the two companies, the operation would boost Parmalat's pre-tax profit by around 17 billion lire ($10 billion), or four percent of Parmalat's consolidated profit," said Marco Opipari, analyst at Intersim brokers.

Parmalat said its own internal 1997 turnover was set to rise 12 percent to 6.1 trillion lire ($3.6 billion) even without Beatrice Foods, but with the Canadian addition it saw turnover at 7.2 trillion lire with a return on sales of over eight percent.

Parmalat reported 1996 results showing annual sales up 27 percent to 5.465 trillion lire, gross operating margins rising 22 percent at 630 billion and net operating margins 27 percent higher at 470 billion. Return on sales was steady at 8.6 percent.
Beatrice Foods had a net operating profit in 1996 of about C$50 million, equal to 5.4 percent of turnover, while it had net financial debt of C$130 million at the end of 1996.
At 1238 GMT, Parmalat was 7.24 percent up at 2,325 lire on a weak bourse after an earlier high of 2,350. Over 12 million shares had changed hands.

"Today's rise shows the market is positive about the deal. There will be synergies and these will be reflected in the share price. Parmalat will be able to get more out of this company," Opipari said.
Beatrice Gerosa, analyst at Banca Commerciale Italiana, said, "notwithstanding today's recovery there could be further room for the share price to firm."

Gerosa, on the basis of Parmalat results and forecasts, saw the new group, including Beatrice Foods, with a 1997 capitalisation rising to 3.88 trillion lire from 3.17 trillion "calculated using Friday's merket prices for Parmalat and with the overall value of the deal for Beatrice which is not quoted."
"Operating profit this year should be around 598 billion lire if we estimate a return on sales of 8.3 percent," she said.

One analyst who preferred not to be named said debt levels were not worrying. "In 1997 the ratio of net financial debt to net equity should be around 70 percent, so there are no big problems," he said. ($=1,192 lire)
